messages:
lumen_poc_contact: Hey team — during our POC today the client is intermittently failing to parse streaming responses. They see partial chunks and sometimes an immediate disconnect. Happens ~1-2x / minute after a few KBs streamed.

sam_sales: ah — thanks for flagging. Are they on our hosted API or Dedicated? Any request IDs?

lumen_poc_contact: Hosted right now, region eu-west-1. No request id in client logs, just client parser errors. We do see a 429 once in a while from the proxy.

alex_engineer: Can you paste a raw capture (curl -v) or the client error text? Also which SDK/lang?

lumen_poc_contact: JS client (EventSource polyfill). Error: `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` while parsing SSE. Here's a short curl run we did:

```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/..."
> GET /v1/streams/... HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
< X-RateLimit-Remaining: 58
< X-RateLimit-Reset: 1672531200
{ [1024 bytes data]
* connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```

But sometimes the body shows truncated event lines like:
```
data: {"id":123,"text":"This is a partial resp"
```
and then immediate socket close from upstream/proxy. Client can't finish event parse.

maria_infra: That looks like proxy buffering/truncation or an upstream worker crash. Two immediate suspects: nginx proxy buffering turning chunk coalescing on, or a 429/limit on our edge causing an abrupt reset.

akash_se: Also could be client parser not tolerant of split UTF-8 / split JSON in SSE. Many clients expect full `\n\n` event terminator. If TCP splits in the middle, polyfills should handle assembly. Does the polyfill buffer incomplete events?

jordan_support: @lumen_poc_contact can you check the browser/Node side network tab for TCP FIN/RESET timing? Is the disconnect client-side or server sent?

lumen_poc_contact: We saw FIN from server side shortly after the partial chunk. No obvious worker crash in their logs. Attached a short server side proxy log snippet:
```
[12:34:21] proxy: upstream_write() returned 0, client: 10.1.2.3, server: api.redwood.ai
[12:34:22] proxy: 502 while reading upstream, client: 10.1.2.3
```

alex_engineer: 502 while reading upstream often means upstream closed connection unexpectedly. We'll check our edge logs for that timeframe. Do you have a reproducible root curl command and an exact timeframe (sec)?

lumen_poc_contact: Repro window 12:34:20-12:34:30 UTC. Repro rate ~1/2 minutes locally.

maria_infra: Quick checklist:\n- confirm `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding off;` for the route\n- ensure `X-Accel-Buffering off` for SSE endpoints\n- verify no intermediate CDN is timing out or applying rate-limit throttles that send TCP resets

akash_se: Another note: our runtime may emit keepalive heartbeats only every 30s. If client expects more frequent bytes and a proxy has a lower idle timeout, proxy may think the connection died and close. Set a short heartbeat (e.g., `":\n"` every 15s) or increase proxy timeout.

sam_sales: Is there a quick mitigation we can apply on hosted side while we debug?

alex_engineer: Yes — we can temporarily toggle route-level proxy buffering off and increase the edge idle timeout for that customer route. I'll push a canary change to eu-west for their org id. Maria: can you apply the nginx config override?

maria_infra: On it. Pushing `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 120s; send_timeout 120s;` to canary.

[~5m later]

maria_infra: Canary applied to lumen org in eu-west. Please retest.

lumen_poc_contact: Retesting now... initial results look promising. Previously failing client parse didn't occur in 5 attempts. Still monitoring.

jordan_support: We should also add resilience notes for them: update EventSource polyfill to buffer until `\n\n` terminator instead of parsing per-chunk, add exponential reconnect on 429/abrupt close, and treat partial JSON across events as normal.

akash_se: Agreed. Also logging: add a `X-Request-Id` in response headers and echo it in event payloads so we can trace specific broken events in future. I'll open an internal ticket to add that to the streaming stack.

alex_engineer: Found a correlated pattern in our edge logs — spikes in `upstream_write() returned 0` aligned with a client sending many concurrent streams from the same org and hitting an internal token bucket. We should throttle per-connection less aggressively or route heavy POC traffic to Dedicated path.

sam_sales: Noted — I'll propose a short-term pricing bump for Dedicated trial to avoid noisy neighbors.

lumen_poc_contact: Thanks everyone — after the canary it's much better. We'll run a 2h soak and report back.

jordan_support: Follow-ups: 
- (ACTION) infra: keep canary config for 48h and collect 5xx/502 counts
- (ACTION) eng: add X-Request-Id and short heartbeat option config for SSE
- (ACTION) solutions: share client-side polyfill doc snippet for robust SSE parsing

streambot: NOTE: ticket #SF-4921 created for tracking, linked to lumen POC.

lumen_poc_contact: Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:. We'll update after soak.
